title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions into parity with current OpenAI semantics. This PR consolidates several behaviour gaps (params validation, role handling, stop sequence and logprobs propagation during streaming, structured/pretty response formatting) and addresses intermittent streaming stability under small-batch workloads.

Summary of changes: added full support for the `roles` field in the chat messages payload and normalized role mapping to internal speaker enums; preserved `stop` sequences semantics and ensured `logprobs` are available when clients request them in streaming mode; stabilized streaming by improving buffer flush heuristics and fixing a race in the streaming encoder; applied consistent response formatting rules (trailing newlines, function-call JSON blob boundaries) to match OpenAI behavior; extended compatibility tests and examples; updated documentation.

Checklist: 
- [x] API behavior parity for params and roles
- [x] Streaming stability fixes and tests
- [x] Preserve stop/logprobs across streaming fragments
- [x] Response formatting parity with OpenAI (including function/tool call marks)
- [x] Integration tests and perf benchmark runs
- [x] Docs updated (docs/openai_compatibility.md)

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover role mapping, stop sequence edge cases, and logprobs passthrough. Integration tests exercised streaming end-to-end with simulated chunk interruptions and verified reconstructed responses and metrics. Perf runs on dedicated pools show improved stability under small-batch traffic (see performance_summary). CI runs passed after addressing a flaky test (`stream_handler_test::partial_flush`). Linked Linear tickets: ENG-1432 (compat parity), ENG-1489 (streaming stability). Related support ticket: SUP-789.

Migration notes: No client-side changes required for backwards compatibility. Customers relying on previous non-standard role names should be informed that upstream mapping enforces `system|user|assistant|tool` canonical roles; deprecated aliases will be accepted for one release and logged as warnings.

Details: see commits and files_changed for the technical breakdown.

release_notes:
- OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: added support for `roles` and stricter params validation.
- Streaming: stable buffer flush and backpressure handling; `logprobs` preserved in streaming responses when requested.
- Response formatting: consistent function-call and tool-call boundaries to match OpenAI behavior.
- Documentation and examples updated.
performance_summary: Reduced mean streaming latency by ~12% on small-batch workloads after buffer flush heuristics change
p99 token latency improved by ~8% on Dedicated pools due to synchronization fix
Net tokens/sec increased ~6% on streaming microbenchmarks; CPU cost delta <1%
changelog_entry: Consolidated OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, and streaming stability fixes. See docs/openai_compatibility.md for migration notes.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout recommended: enable on 10% of traffic for 24h and monitor streaming_metrics.prom:streaming_partial_retries and api.error.rates. If increased partial_retries or function-call truncation is observed, rollback to previous release and contact authors.

from redwood import OpenAICompat
client = OpenAICompat()
resp = client.chat_completions.create(model="redwood-alpha-1", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count to 3"}], stream=True, logprobs=5, stop=["
"])
